trust_decision.summary: Whether a path listed in a policy group's deny.access is actually unreachable is decided on Linux by the caller-invoked check validate_deny_overlaps, which ignores exact-path overlaps and non-user-sourced grants, and is never consulted at the sandbox-apply sink.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'authorization bypass / policy confusion' in the summary goes to policy resolution; validate_deny_overlaps is the only code in the tree that decides whether a deny rule is enforceable.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: resolve_deny_paths/resolve_groups only report expanded path strings; a solver can argue their job is reporting, so the missing enforcement belongs solely to validate_deny_overlaps and to the application that calls it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The embedded profile deliberately grants read to $HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db (claude_code_macos, codex_macos) inside the tree that deny_keychains_macos denies whole; a 'deny always wins' rule applied outside the macOS Seatbelt path rejects the project's own shipped policy, and the unlink deny plus unlink_override_for_user_writable pair is the same shape.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: data/policy.json:33-48 with data/policy.json:403-411; see also data/policy.json:473-479 and src/policy.rs:442-466
